title: one-minute-action-templates-scratchpad
content:
Context / why this idea: quick wins for users — tiny prebuilt assistant actions that take <60s to complete (ask + result). We want low-friction discovery + low token cost so people feel value immediately and then customize. Think: 1-click resume summary, short code refactor suggestion, meeting note extraction, SQL-from-csv example.

Goals (hypothesis):
- Increase time-to-value for new users; first meaningful action should be under 1 minute from signup.
- Provide composable, saveable templates that teams can adapt and share.
- Keep per-action token cost low (target median < 150 tokens).
- Surface premium/Dedicated-friendly templates separately (enterprise-ready with data connectors).

Primary persona(s):
- Product Engineer (first-time explorer of Redwood API / Console)
- Customer Success / Solutions Engineer who demos quick features
- Knowledge worker who wants fast productivity helpers inside their app

Core idea: one-minute-action templates (OMATs) = small prompt+tool presets + minimal UX shell. Each template includes: title, short instruction, required inputs (1-3), optional context toggles (tone/length), default model variant (cheap/fast), and expected token budget.

Example templates (seed list):
- "TL;DR Resume": paste job description + resume -> 3 bullets tailored match (model: gpt-x-small, budget 120 tokens)
- "SQL Quick Query": upload sample CSV or paste headers -> generate 1 SQL query and brief explanation (model: sql-fast-quant, budget 100)
- "Meeting Highlights": paste transcript -> 5 highlight bullets + action items (model: conv-compact, budget 200)
- "Refactor Hint": paste <100 lines of code -> 3 targeted suggestions + cost/risk note (model: code-lite, budget 150)

User stories (rough):
- As a new user, I can run a "TL;DR Resume" template from the dashboard and immediately get 3 bullets to paste in an application.
- As a solutions engineer, I can duplicate and edit an OMAT, then share a link to the edited template with a customer.
- As a product owner, I can see per-template usage and token cost in Console.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Console: small gallery of 6 curated OMATs with preview + run button.
- API: /templates endpoint that returns template metadata; /templates/:id/run that accepts required inputs and returns structured output.
- Cost control defaults: each template chooses a model tier (fast/cheap or high-fidelity) and exposes a max-token cap.
- Save/duplicate flow: user can clone templates into their workspace and edit instructions/inputs.

UX sketches (notes to self):
- Gallery card = name, 1-line intent, estimated token cost, run CTA, little lightning icon for <1min claim.
- Run modal = input field(s) + sample content toggles + small slider for fidelity vs cost (mapped to model choice).
- Result card = collapsible; show token usage + model name; quick "save as template" with name.

Metrics / how we measure success:
- Activation: % of new signups who run at least one OMAT in first 7 days (target 35% -> 50% pilot).
- Retention: share of users who save a template after running >=1 (target 8%).
- Cost: median tokens per run (target <150).
- Latency: p50 response time for OMAT runs (target <400ms for local small models, <800ms for larger).
- Demo adoption: number of internal demo decks using OMAT flows.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (prototype): local-only small gallery in internal console + hand-run via postman. Collect feedback. (owner: me)
- Phase 1 (public beta): public gallery + API endpoints, analytics. Test on hosted API with cost caps. (owner: product-hosted-api)
- Phase 2 (enterprise): templates with connectors (S3/Sheets) and Private-ready templates for Dedicated/Private. (owner: solutions-engineering)

Risk and tradeoffs:
- Risk: cheap templates degrade perceived quality if output is weak -> mitigations: curated prompts, examples, and explicit fidelity toggle.
- Risk: template proliferation -> mitigation: allow team-scoped visibility, pinning, and an approval workflow.
- Latency vs cost tension: surface simple defaults but allow power users to switch models.

Open questions / TODOs: (short list)
- What is the creator UX for required inputs (free text vs file upload vs structured fields)?
- Can templates ship with small client-side pre-validation to reduce model calls?
- How to represent multi-step templates (e.g., extract -> summarize -> rewrite) without confusing users?
- Analytics: what taxonomy do we use for templates in telemetry (category, use-case)?

Next steps (this week):
- Prototype run flow in Console (Talia + me) -> simple modal + 3 templates.
- Add minimal /templates API schema proposal and share in #product-templates. (Ishaan)
- Put rough cost budgets per template and run a cost sim for 1k runs/month at different mixes (Mika).

Notes / stray thoughts:
- Consider a "micro-credits" UX: small free quota for first 10 OMAT runs to show quick wins.
- Could be powerful lead-gen: prebuilt templates for verticals (recruiting, sales ops) with example inputs.
- If we expose a fidelity slider, we should translate into plain language: "faster/cheaper" vs "detailed/accurate" + expected cost estimate.

Quick links:
- slack: #templates-ideas thread -> slack.com/archives/C12345 (TODO paste link)
- existing sandbox: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/omat-sandbox

Parking-lot (future):
- Template marketplace with curated partner templates.
- Template schema versioning and diff view for rollouts.
- Template-level A/B experiments to test different prompt variants.

End of notes. This is intentionally rough — want to capture momentum and get a tiny prototype in front of users fast.
